memories.content: Mark unverified schedule assumptions as such.
Mark unverified recruitment assumptions as such.
Mark unverified technical assumptions as such.
Clarify which stage of prototype fabrication or user study each requested resource is used for.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the personnel assigned to each procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the equipment assigned to each procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the time allocated to each procedure.
Verify that the planned number of formative evaluation iterations is feasible within the time for prototype modification and recruitment resources.
Include only the minimum functionality required to compare primary design assumptions in the scope of the formative evaluation prototype.
The user's iterative design plan can be judged feasible only if time and personnel are allocated for modifying the prototype between iterations.
Delays in participant recruitment can compress the time available for prototype modification between formative evaluations.
Specify field and user data sources and analysis procedures corresponding to all HCI research questions.
In preregistered studies, clarify the criteria for judging plan changes.
In preregistered studies, clarify the location for recording plan changes.
Use a justified minimum-to-maximum target range when confirmations can change, and tie the minimum and maximum to different workload and budget cases.
Specify the observation records, system logs, or interview tools used to collect each type of field and user data.
Specify whether each type of field and user data will be collected before, during, or after deployment.
Readers cannot assess a target range unless both bounds have a stated consequence for schedule, workload, or cost.
In field deployments, network and service instability exist as independent causes of task failure alongside design choices.
If a safety signal occurs in the field system, existing institutional safety procedures take precedence over the research schedule and data collection plan.
Reviewers judge answerability by tracing the path from each research question to its data sources and analysis procedures.
The user authoring this proposal tends to present implemented feature lists directly as design contributions.
Define what can still be completed at the minimum target instead of treating every number inside the range as operationally identical.
Use a bounded range to absorb expected confirmation changes without pretending that one early estimate is guaranteed.
Show how session count and facilitator time change at the minimum and maximum bounds.
Define the additional workload or deliverable enabled at the maximum target so the upper bound is not an arbitrary cushion.
A bounded range preserves uncertainty honestly but makes the final workload and budget less certain than one fixed target.

analysis.overview: The frames cover different proposal-review concerns. Reference concentrates on exposing assumptions and testing prototype-iteration feasibility through scoped resources, timing, recruitment, and minimal functionality; Compared concentrates on research answerability, preregistration changes, bounded targets, field failure and safety, and contribution framing.

relations.reason: These Memories split one reference-only disclosure rule by assumption category; the Compared frame contains no corresponding assumption-labeling policy.
relations.summary: Unverified schedule, recruitment, and technical assumptions should be explicitly identified as unverified.

relations.reason: This is a reference-only requirement for stage-specific resource justification, not the same decision as the Compared frame’s data-method or target-range requirements.
relations.summary: Each requested resource should be tied to the prototype-fabrication or user-study stage where it is used.

relations.reason: These Memories split one reference-only feasibility criterion across three resource dimensions; no Compared Memory states that procedure-level criterion.
relations.summary: Procedure feasibility is judged from its assigned personnel, equipment, and time.

relations.reason: Both Memories express parts of one reference-only capacity test for iterative evaluation; the Compared frame does not address between-iteration prototype modification.
relations.summary: Formative iteration feasibility depends on adequate prototype-modification time and supporting personnel or recruitment capacity.

relations.reason: This reference-only prototype-scoping rule is operationally independent of the Compared frame’s observation, target-setting, and contribution-framing claims.
relations.summary: A formative-evaluation prototype should contain only the minimum functionality needed to compare primary design assumptions.

relations.reason: This reference-only causal schedule risk is independently useful and is not stated by the Compared frame.
relations.summary: Participant-recruitment delays can reduce the time available for prototype modification between formative evaluations.

relations.reason: These Compared Memories restate and decompose one question-to-data-and-analysis traceability requirement; the Reference frame contains no corresponding research-method pathway.
relations.summary: HCI research questions should trace to specified field or user data sources, collection instruments and timing, and analysis procedures so their answerability can be assessed.

relations.reason: These Compared Memories split one change-governance requirement into decision and documentation components; the Reference frame does not address preregistration changes.
relations.summary: Preregistered studies should define both the criteria for judging plan changes and where those changes will be recorded.

relations.reason: These Compared Memories state, justify, and decompose one policy for operationally meaningful target ranges; the Reference frame has no bounded-target policy.
relations.summary: When confirmations may change, a bounded target should state distinct minimum and maximum consequences for deliverables, sessions, workload, schedule, or budget while acknowledging remaining uncertainty.

relations.reason: This Compared-only attribution consideration is not addressed by the Reference frame’s prototype and recruitment feasibility claims.
relations.summary: Network and service instability are independent potential causes of task failure in field deployments, separate from design choices.

relations.reason: This Compared-only safety precedence rule governs a distinct field contingency absent from the Reference frame.
relations.summary: A field-system safety signal makes institutional safety procedures take precedence over the research schedule and data-collection plan.

relations.reason: This Compared-only authoring diagnosis concerns contribution framing and has no counterpart in the Reference frame.
relations.summary: The proposal author tends to present lists of implemented features directly as design contributions.

reports.compared_only: Compared alone addresses question-to-data traceability, preregistration change records, operationally meaningful target ranges, infrastructure-caused field failures, safety precedence, and a tendency to mistake implemented features for design contributions.
reports.reference_only: Reference alone addresses assumption labeling, stage-specific resources, procedure and iteration feasibility, minimal prototype scope, and recruitment delays that erode modification time.
